title: Preserving Heisenberg-Limited Metrological Information during Storage via Correlated-Noise Correction
authors: Hang Xu, Xue-Ke Song, Jingzheng Huang, Tailong Xiao, Guihua Zeng
abstract: Quantum error correction has become an indispensable tool for restoring Heisenberg-limited precision in noisy quantum metrology. Existing protocols, however, almost exclusively focus on correcting noise during the signal-encoding stage and implicitly assume that the probe is measured immediately after sensing. In many quantum information processing tasks, the encoded probe must instead be stored before subsequent quantum operations, during which environmental noise can significantly degrade the accumulated metrological information. Here, we propose a correlated-noise correction (CNC) protocol for protecting quantum probes during the storage stage. By correlating probe errors with auxiliary qubits through fixed two-body entangling gates, memory errors are converted into measurable syndromes that are extracted only once after storage. We show that the protocol naturally extends from single-qubit to multi-qubit probes and protects the stored quantum Fisher information against dephasing, bit-flip, and amplitude-damping noise. Furthermore, we demonstrate that preserving the quantum Fisher information does not necessarily require restoring the entire quantum state when the probe is measured immediately after storage, whereas full state recovery becomes essential for subsequent rounds of quantum signal processing. Our results establish correlated-noise correction as a practical framework for protecting metrological information during quantum memory and provide a useful building block for sensing-enabled quantum information processing.
summary: The paper introduces Correlated-Noise Correction (CNC), a novel protocol designed to protect high-precision metrological information stored in noisy quantum memories. By entangling the probe with auxiliary qubits, environmental errors are mapped into measurable syndromes that can be read out post-storage. This framework proves vital for building practical quantum sensors capable of operating over extended periods.
main_problem: The primary challenge is preserving Heisenberg-limited metrological information encoded during a sensing stage when the quantum probe must be stored in a noisy environment before subsequent measurements or operations.
main_result: A Correlated-Noise Correction (CNC) protocol was proposed that protects the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) against various noise types during storage without requiring full state recovery unless further processing is needed.
method: The CNC protocol correlates memory errors on the probe with auxiliary qubits using fixed two-body entangling gates, converting environmental decoherence into measurable syndromes extracted only after the storage period.
model_or_system: The model involves a quantum probe undergoing sensing followed by storage in a noisy channel. The framework is generalized from single-qubit to multi-qubit systems and applies to various noise types like dephasing, bit-flip, and amplitude damping.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), which serves as the figure of merit for sensing precision; Mean-Square Estimation Error (MSE).
important_parameters: Storage time ($t_m$), sensing time ($t_s$), noise types (dephasing, bit-flip, amplitude damping).
main_assumptions: The sensing stage is assumed to be protected by existing QEC or that the storage time is much longer than the sensing time; full state recovery is only necessary if the probe is reused for subsequent signal accumulation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the general CNC framework (entanglement gates before and inverse gates after memory), showing QFI preservation under dephasing noise, comparison of QFI vs. storage time, and demonstration of continuous QFI accumulation over multiple sensing-storage rounds.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem gap in existing error correction methods, proposes the CNC protocol by correlating errors with auxiliary qubits, demonstrates its efficacy for various noise channels (single/multi-qubit), and concludes by distinguishing between QFI preservation and full state recovery requirements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical limitations of quantum metrology in real-world settings where measurement cannot be instantaneous, providing a robust theoretical tool for memory management in quantum sensing architectures.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. General framework of the correlated-noise correc- tion (CNC) protocol. Before the memory stage, each auxil- iary qubit is entangled with the probe through a two-body gate Ti. During the memory process, probe errors are co- herently correlated with the corresponding auxiliary qubits. After storage, the inverse gates T † i transform the accumulated probe errors into measurable auxiliary syndromes, which are extracted by measuring the auxiliary qubits. The probe itself is never measured during the memory process.

FIG. 2. Performance of the CNC protocol for a single- qubit probe subject to dephasing noise during the memory stage. (a) QFI as a function of the memory time tm for a fixed sensing time ts = 10, where different curves correspond to different dephasing rates of the auxiliary qubit. (b) QFI as a function of the sensing time ts for a fixed memory time tm = 20. The black dashed line denotes the ideal noiseless result.

FIG. 3. Performance of the CNC protocol for a memory channel containing simultaneous bit-flip and dephasing noise. (a) QFI versus the memory time tm for a fixed sensing time ts = 10. The inset shows the fidelity between the stored probe state and the corresponding noiseless state. (b) QFI versus the sensing time ts for a fixed memory time tm = 20. Results obtained by correcting only the dephasing noise are compared with those obtained by correcting both noise channels and with the ideal noiseless case.

FIG. 4. Performance of the CNC protocol for amplitude- damping noise during the memory stage. (a) QFI as a func- tion of the memory time tm for a fixed sensing time ts = 10. (b) QFI as a function of the sensing time ts for a fixed mem- ory time tm = 20. The corrected protocol is compared with the uncorrected protocol and the ideal noiseless limit.

FIG. 5. Two-qubit CNC for a single sensing-storage cycle with local dephasing noise during the memory stage. (a) QFI as a function of memory time for a fixed sensing duration. (b) MSE as a function of the number of measurement shots after the storage stage. The CNC protocol is compared with the uncorrected and noise-free cases.
